mappings.note: Ambedkar as father of the Constitution. A fact about how the Constitution was framed; no LO covers its making, so the goal on understanding the Constitution is cited rather than C-SST5.1-LO-2, which is about illustrating rights.
Taxes and defence sit on the Union List; the division of subjects between the two levels is exactly what C-SST5.2-LO-1 asks to be differentiated.
First Indian Governor General; a transitional constitutional office with no outcome of its own -> goal-level.
Potti Sriramulu's fast for a Telugu state is a regional political issue settled under the Constitution -> C-SST5.1-LO-1, not the rights outcome.
Date the Constitution came into force -> goal-level; no LO covers constitutional chronology.
Andhra Pradesh formed on 1 October 1953; linguistic state reorganisation, a regional political issue under the Constitution -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Year the Planning Commission was set up; an institution of the Indian state, so goal-level, since no LO reaches economic planning bodies.
India's first Prime Minister; the head of the Union executive is one of the institutions the goal names, and no LO covers office-holders.
First woman Chief Minister; a state-government office. Not C-SST5.2-LO-1, which asks for the difference between the two levels, not who held an office.
What the Concurrent List covers; the three-list split is the core of differentiating State from Union government -> C-SST5.2-LO-1.
Chairman of the Drafting Committee; constitution-making -> goal-level.
First Deputy Prime Minister; a Union office -> goal-level.
Bombay split into Marathi and Gujarati states in 1960; linguistic reorganisation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Opposition to imposing Hindi on South India; a regional political and language issue framed by the Constitution -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Mysore as the older name of Karnataka; state reorganisation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Punjab divided into Punjab and Haryana in 1966; state reorganisation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Old name of Madhya Pradesh; state reorganisation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
First Foreign Minister; a Union office -> goal-level, as with the other office-holder items.
Where the Constituent Assembly met; constitution-making -> goal-level.
Who Potti Sriramulu was; the linguistic-state agitation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.

Describing the practice of untouchability -> C-SST6.1-LO-2, which names Scheduled Castes. C-SST5.1-LO-2 was considered, but the item asks about the social practice rather than about illustrating the Fundamental Right that abolishes it.
The Congress promise of the 1920s to redraw provinces on linguistic lines; the origin of the reorganisation issue -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Size of the Constituent Assembly; constitution-making -> goal-level.
What the Union List is -> C-SST5.2-LO-1, the State/Union division.
How long princely states stayed as administrative units; the integration of states before reorganisation -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
The term for the right to vote is universal adult franchise; an electoral principle -> C-SST5.2-LO-2 (election to the Lok Sabha), not C-SST5.1-LO-2, since voting is not a Fundamental Right.
Year the States Reorganisation Committee was set up -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Best description of universal adult franchise -> C-SST5.2-LO-2, the franchise underpinning Lok Sabha elections.
Who else received reservation alongside the Untouchables (Scheduled Tribes) -> C-SST6.1-LO-2, which names Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Year Punjab was divided (duplicate theme of qid:110810) -> C-SST5.1-LO-1.
Who said 'one caste, one religion, one god for humankind'; caste-equality reform -> C-SST6.1-LO-2, the human-rights outcome covering Scheduled Castes.
Who first demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1934; constitution-making -> goal-level.
Who drafted the Constitution -> goal-level.
When Nepal's democracy struggle began; the chapter's comparative case for why a country needs a constitution -> goal-level, since no LO covers other countries.
Father of the Constitution (duplicate of qid:110789) -> goal-level.
What the Constitution introduced for economic and social reform (the Directive Principles); a feature of the Constitution rather than a Fundamental Right, so goal-level and not C-SST5.1-LO-2.
The executive named as those who implement laws and run the government; an organ of the state -> goal-level, since no LO covers the separation of organs.
Jagjivan Ram as India's first Labour Minister; a Union office -> goal-level.
More than one level of government is federalism; the concept C-SST5.2-LO-1's State/Union differentiation rests on.
Trafficking and forced labour are barred by the Right against Exploitation -> C-SST5.1-LO-2, illustrating a Fundamental Right.
The form of India's government; a characterisation of the constitutional system as a whole -> goal-level, since the option could be parliamentary or federal and neither LO settles it.
Freedom of movement falls under the Right to Freedom -> C-SST5.1-LO-2.

The courts collectively are the judiciary. C-SST6.2-LO-1 is about expressing views on judges' role and LO-2 is the FIR form, so the competency that describes the judiciary is the right level for a definitional item.
India's first Finance Minister; a Union office -> goal-level.
